p.seg: *Féng Yù Piān* (Chapter on Fortuitous Encounters)
*Cāoxíng* (moral conduct) has constant worth,
official careers have inconstant encounters.
Whether one is worthy or unworthy
is a matter of talent;
whether one encounters opportunity or not
is a matter of time.
High talent and pure conduct
cannot guarantee certain honor and nobility;
meager abilities and sullied morals
cannot guarantee certain baseness and lowliness.
Perhaps those with high talent and pure conduct,
If not encountered (by a ruler),
To be relegated to the lower stream;
With meager ability, to muddy one's integrity;
To be favored,
is to be above the masses.
Each age has its own way of selecting scholars,
and scholars also each have their own way of advancing.
Advancement depends on favor,
retreat depends on lack of favor.
To occupy a position of honor and prominence
does not necessarily mean one is virtuous,
it is due to being favored;
to be in a humble position below
does not necessarily mean one is foolish,
it is due to lack of favor.
Therefore, when favored,
one might embrace corrupt conduct
and be more respected than in the court of Jié:
When not favored,
one might uphold pure integrity
and be lower than in the court of Yáo.
The reasons for being favored or not favored
are not uniform:
Sometimes one is truly virtuous but assists evil;
sometimes one uses great talent to follow lesser talent;
sometimes both have great talent, but their paths differ in purity;
sometimes one lacks morals but is suitable due to their skills;
sometimes one lacks skills but gains favor due to their beauty.
Wǔ Yuán, Bó Xǐ,
both served Fūchāi.
Bó Xǐ was respected,
Wǔ Yuán was executed.
This is a case of different conduct under the same ruler.
Or, there are cases of the same conduct under different rulers,
with varying fortune,
Yī Yǐn and Jī Zǐ are examples of this.
Yī Yǐn and Jī Zǐ, their talents were the same,
Yī Yǐn became prime minister,
Jī Zǐ became a slave;
Yī Yǐn met Chéng Tāng,
Jī Zǐ met Shāng Zhòu.
When a worthy serves a worthy ruler,
and the ruler desires to govern well,
the minister assists him with his talent,
their tendencies and preferences coinciding,
their success is naturally appropriate.
When a worthy serves an evil ruler,
and the ruler does not desire to govern well,
the minister assists him with loyal conduct,
their conduct and ambitions clashing,
their failure is naturally appropriate.
Or, sometimes a worthy and sage minister
encounters a ruler who desires to govern well,
yet ultimately meets with misfortune,
Kǒngzǐ and Mèng Kē are examples of this.
Kǒngzǐ ran out of provisions in Chén and Cài,
Mèng Kē was stuck in Qí and Liáng.
It's not that the rulers of those times did not want to use good men,
but that their talent and knowledge were shallow,
and they were unable to employ great talents.
For the one who can control excellent steeds,
must be Wang Liang;
those who can employ Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao as ministers,
must be Yao and Shun.
Using a hand capable of maneuvering within a hundred *li*,
to control feet capable of traveling a thousand *li*,
there will inevitably be the danger of breaking the yoke and snapping the harness;
having the talent to manage common subjects,
and using it to control the wisdom of great ministers,
there will inevitably be a transformation of closed minds and blocked intentions.
Therefore, the most profound words are discarded,
and sages and worthies are resisted,
not because they are hated,
but because the profound words are unpalatable.
Sages and worthies strive for loftiness,
and profound words are difficult to put into practice.
Now, when great talent tries to interact with small talent,
the small talent cannot accept it,
so it is only natural that it is not encountered/accepted.
Or, when a minister of great talent,
encounters a ruler of great talent,
there can still be instances of being encountered or not encountered.
Yú Shùn, Xǔ Yóu, Tàigōng, and Bó Yí are examples of this.
Yú Shùn and
Xǔ Yóu were both sages.
They both lived during the Táng dynasty,
and both were presented before Yáo.
Afterwards, no one recommended him,
yet he still obtained an official position.
Why is that?
Because the omen had already appeared,
and its fulfillment was certain.
In ancient times, years were called *líng* (age),
having already reached nine *líng*,
was like a person dreaming of obtaining a noble rank.
Because Zhōu Gōng took the dream that was sure to come true,
and requested it from Heaven,
how could his merit be small?"
Someone then asked:
"Merit has no large or small,
virtue has no much or little,
people must have someone to look up to and rely on,
then it is good.
If Zhōu Gōng had not substituted for Wǔ Wáng,
and Wǔ Wáng had died of illness,
could Zhōu Gōng and Chéng Wáng have brought about peace and stability to the world?"
He replied:
"It would have been accomplished,
Zhōu Gōng assisted Chéng Wáng and the world would not have been in chaos.
If Wǔ Wáng had not been substituted for,
and consequently died of illness,
is there any doubt that Zhōu Gōng could have brought about peace and stability?"
Someone challenged:
"If that is the case,
Wǔ Wáng's life was of no benefit,
and his death was of no loss,
Zhōu Gōng's merit was necessary for success.
When the Zhōu dynasty declined,
the feudal lords rebelled,
Guǎn Zhòng united the feudal lords nine times,
and rectified the whole world.
Confucius said:
'Without Guǎn Zhòng,
I would be wearing my hair loose and fastening my robes on the left.'
If there had been no Guǎn Zhòng,
and the feudal lords had not been united,
the barbarians would have invaded in waves,
the Central Kingdom would have been annihilated,
this is what the loss of Guǎn Zhòng would have harmed.
Making calculations is beneficial,
the merit of Guǎn Zhòng,
is on par with that of the Duke of Zhou.
When Guǎn Zhòng died,
Duke Huán did not bury him with the rites due to a feudal lord,
comparing him to the Duke of Zhou,
Heaven should have been angry,
why were there no faint thunder and light rain?
Why?
Was it because the Duke of Zhou was a sage while Guǎn Zhòng was not virtuous?
Now, Guǎn Zhòng built a *fǎn diàn*,
and had three returning wives (*sān guī*),
Confucius criticized him for this,
(Someone) thought he was not virtuous.
"Returning the goblet stand,"
"Three Returns,"
are the rites of the feudal lords;
"A Son of Heaven's funeral rites,"
are the regulations of a true king,
all of which, as a subject,
he may not perform.
A great man's virtue aligns with Heaven and Earth.
Confucius,
was a great man,
and he criticized Guǎn Zhòng for overstepping the rites.
(If) Heaven desired Zhōu Gōng's transgression of the regulations,
this is not proof of aligning virtue.
The explanation of the scholars of the *Book of Documents*,
is not acceptable."
To see bird tracks and then know how to write,
to see tumbling weeds and then know how to make a cart,
Heaven did not instruct Cāngjié with bird tracks,
or send Xī Zhòng because of the tumbling weeds.
Xī Zhòng was inspired by the tumbling weeds,
and Cāngjié was inspired by the bird tracks.
When Duke Wén of Jìn returned to his state,
he ordered the removal of the painted chariot,
Jiù Fàn felt deeply moved,
and resigned from his position to return home.
Now, Duke Wén's removal of the painted chariot,
(It was) not that (he) wanted to remove Jiùfàn;
Jiùfàn felt ashamed,
and voluntarily associated himself with the commoners.
Huáchén of Sòng weakened his clan,
and employed six domestic thieves,
who killed Huá Wú with pī-spears behind the zuǒshī (Left Commander) of Sòng at Hé.
The zuǒshī was afraid and said:
"This old man is innocent."
Afterwards, the zuǒshī resented Huáchén,
and Huáchén prepared for him.
The people of the state were chasing a mad dog,
and the mad dog entered the gate of Huáchén's house.
Huáchén thought that the zuǒshī had come to attack him,
and fled over the wall.
Huáchén himself killed Huá Wú, yet the zuǒshī was afraid;
the people of the state themselves chased a mad dog, yet Huáchén himself fled.
The fear of King Chéng,
was similar to this.
He suspected in his heart that he had not buried the Duke with the rites due to the Son of Heaven,
and finally encountered the arrival of thunder and rain,
so he was overly fearful and apprehensive.
The arrival of thunder and rain,
was not necessarily Heaven blaming King Chéng.
The thunder and rain arrived,
and King Chéng was afraid and blamed himself.
To be moved is like the mind of Cāngjié,
or Xīzhòng.
To be fearful is like the zuǒshī,
This is what Huá Chén meant.
Harboring plans of suspicion,
encountering the energy of sudden arrival,
when verification is seen through analogous things,
then the effect of Heaven's anger is achieved.
Seeing verification from similar things in silence and solitude,
one still feels moved and fearful,
how much more so when the thunder and rain raise booming sounds!
Can King Chéng possibly not be frightened?
When there is swift thunder and violent wind,
Kǒng Zǐ certainly changes his countenance.
According to the Rites, when a gentleman hears thunder,
even at night,
he puts on his clothes and cap and sits up,
this is to show respect for the thunder and fear the excited energy.
Sages and gentlemen have no doubt about the Dao,
yet they still follow Heaven's changes and movements,
how much more so when King Chéng suspects Zhōu Gōng,
when he hears the changes of thunder and rain,
how can he not be alarmed and fearful?
Therefore, the arrival of thunder and rain
almost certainly comes from the weather;
King Chéng's fear
almost certainly comes from perceiving the categories of things.
The Dao of Heaven is non-action.
If Heaven uses thunder and rain to angrily rebuke people,
then it can also use thunder and rain to kill the wicked.
Ancient rulers who lacked virtue were many.
If Heaven could punish them with thunder and lightning,
why would it necessarily command sages to raise armies and mobilize troops,
causing armies to be stalled and soldiers to be injured?
If it's difficult to carry out punishment with a single thunderbolt,
and easy to defeat enemies with three armies,
why would Heaven not be afraid of trouble?
Someone might say:
"Zhòu's 紂 father, Dì Yǐ 帝乙,
shot at the sky and beat the ground,
roaming between the Hé 河 and
Wèi 渭 Rivers,
and was struck and killed by thunder and lightning.
This is Heaven punishing the wicked with thunder and lightning."
But the evil of Dì Yǐ 帝乙,
compared to that of Jié 桀 and Zhòu 紂,
Zōu Bóqí 鄒伯奇 argued that the evil of Jié 桀 and Zhòu 紂 was not as great as that of the fallen Qín 秦,
and the fallen Qín 秦 was not as great as that of Wáng Mǎng 王莽.
However, the deaths of Jié 桀, Zhòu 紂, Qín 秦, and Mǎng 莽
did not involve thunder and lightning.
Confucius, in writing the *Chūnqiū 春秋* (Spring and Autumn Annals),
selected even the slightest good,
and disparaged even the tiniest evil,
selecting good without exaggerating its beauty,
and disparaging evil without exceeding its transgression.
To blame a small thing with great consequence
no man will do.
King Chéngwáng 成王 had a small doubt,
To blame the small with the standard of the great,
no one does that.
King Chéng had a small doubt,
and heaven responded with great thunder and rain.
If even the burial of a duke by his subject can be settled,
what change could exceed this?
The "Hóng Fàn" investigates doubts,
but those who don't understand calamities and changes
simply lack the ability to fully comprehend them.
Heaven doesn't blame people for not being able to resolve every doubt.
King Chéng's heart was hesitant and unresolved,
and heaven blamed him with great thunder and rain.
That probably wasn't the intention of Imperial Heaven.
The interpretations of the "Book" scholars
probably miss the truth.
The "Qí Shì Piān"
says that people of the upper ages
were large and tall, fine and handsome,
strong and long-lived,
living to be around a hundred years old;
people of the lower ages
are short and small, ugly and deformed,
and die young and prematurely.
Why is this?
The upper ages had harmonious and pure atmospheres,
marriages occurred at the proper time,
and the people were born with good qi,
Being born without injury,
with firm bones and joints,
therefore one grows up to a long and healthy old age,
with a beautiful appearance.
The opposite is true in later generations,
therefore one is short, small, and dies young,
with an ugly appearance.
This is a false statement.
Those who governed in earlier ages were sages (shèngrén),
were also sages (shèngrén).
Those who governed in later ages
were also sages (shèngrén).
The virtue of sages (shèngrén),
does not differ from past to present,
therefore their governance of the world
is no different from ancient to modern times.
The heaven of earlier ages
is the heaven of later ages,
Heaven does not change,
and the qi (qì) does not alter.
The people of earlier ages
are the people of later ages,
all endowed with primordial qi (yuánqì).
Primordial qi (yuánqì) is pure and harmonious,
and has not differed from ancient to modern times,
therefore those who are endowed with it to form their bodies,
why are they different?
If their received *qi* is equal,
then their inherent nature will be uniform.
If their inherent nature is uniform,
then their physical forms will be the same.
If their physical forms are the same,
then ugliness and beauty will be equal.
If ugliness and beauty are equal,
then premature death and long life will be appropriate.
One heaven and one earth
together produce myriad things.
The birth of myriad things
all receive one *qi*.
The thinness or thickness of this *qi*,
is seemingly the same for ten thousand generations.
Emperors govern the world,
for a hundred generations they follow the same path.
The people marry,
observing the same rites at the same time,
although it is said that men marry at thirty,
and women marry at twenty,
legal regulations are established,
but they are not necessarily followed.
How can we verify this?
Because they are not followed today.
The system of ritual and music
exists and is seen today,
but do the people of today
willingly practice them?
Modern people are unwilling to practice it,
and the ancients were also unwilling to promote it.
Using the people of today
to understand the people of ancient times.
People
are things,
and things are also things.
A person lives in the world
to a life span of one hundred years.
When one is born as a ten-year-old child,
of the things seen on the earth,
many undergo birth, death, change, and alteration.
As for reaching one hundred years,
when one is about to die,
the various things seen
are no different from what one saw at the age of ten.
There is no difference.
If those in the upper generations and the lower generations,
the people are not different,
then the time between one hundred years
is enough to divine the future.
The height and size of the six domestic animals,
the size of the five grains,
insects, grasses, and trees,
gold, stones, pearls, and jade,
tiny flying and wriggling creatures,
those that crawl and those that breathe with a beak,
無有異者， There is nothing different.
此形不異也。 This form is not different.
古之水火、 The water and fire of ancient times,
今之水火也。 are the water and fire of today.
今氣為水火也， Today's *qì* becomes water and fire.
使氣有異， If the *qì* were different,
則古之水清火熱， then would the water of ancient times be clear and the fire hot,
而今水濁火寒乎？ and the water of today be turbid and the fire cold?
人生長六七尺， A person is born and grows to six or seven *chǐ*,
大三四圍， with a girth of three or four *wéi*,
面有五色， a face with five colors,
壽至於百， and a lifespan reaching a hundred years—
萬世不異。 for ten thousand generations, this is not different.
如以上世人民， If the people of previous ages
侗長佼好， were exceptionally tall and beautiful,
堅彊老壽， strong and long-lived,
下世反此， and later generations were the opposite,
則天地初立， then when heaven and earth were first established,
始為人時， when people first came into being,
長可如Fángfēng zhī Jūn, could their height have been like that of the lord of Fángfēng,
色如Sòng Cháo， their complexion like Sòng Cháo,
壽如Péngzǔ乎？ their lifespan like Péngzǔ's?
從當今至千世之後， From the present day to a thousand generations hence,
人可長如莢英， could people be as tall as a *jiá yīng* (small pod),
色如Mómǔ， their complexion like Mómǔ's,
壽如朝生乎？ their lifespan like that of a morning glory?
Wáng Mǎng之時， During the time of Wáng Mǎng,
長人生長一丈， a very tall person was one *zhàng* tall,
名曰霸出。 míng yuē Bà Chū. It is named "Bà Chū."
建武年中， Jiànwǔ nián zhōng, During the Jiànwǔ reign period (25-56 AD),
潁川張仲師長二尺二寸。 Yǐngchuān Zhāng Zhòngshī zhǎng èr chǐ èr cùn. Zhāng Zhòngshī of Yǐngchuān was two chi and two cun tall.
張湯八尺有餘， Zhāng Tāng bā chǐ yǒuyú, Zhāng Tāng was over eight chi tall,
其父不滿五尺。 qí fù bù mǎn wǔ chǐ. while his father was less than five chi.
俱在今世， jū zài jīnshì, Both are alive in the present age.
或長或短， huò cháng huò duǎn, Some are tall, some are short.
儒者之言， Rúzhě zhī yán, The words of the Confucian scholars
竟非誤也。 jìng fēi wù yě. are not at all mistaken.
語稱上世使民以宜， yǔ chēng shàngshì shǐ mín yǐ yí, It is said that in ancient times, people were employed according to their suitability;
傴者抱關， yǔ zhě bào guān, hunchbacks guarded the gates,
侏儒俳優。 zhūrú pāiyōu. and dwarfs were performers.
如皆侗長佼好， rú jiē tóng cháng jiǎo hǎo, If everyone were tall and handsome,
安得傴、 ān dé yǔ, where would one get the hunchbacks
侏之人乎？ zhū zhī rén hū? and dwarfs?
語稱上世之人， yǔ chēng shàngshì zhī rén, It is said that the people of ancient times
質朴易化； zhìpǔ yì huà; were simple and easy to transform;
下世之人， xiàshì zhī rén, but the people of later ages
文薄難治。 wén bó nán zhì. are cultured but shallow and difficult to govern.
故《易》曰： gù "Yì" yuē: Therefore, the *Book of Changes* says:
「上古之時結繩以治， "shànggǔ zhī shí jié shéng yǐ zhì, "In ancient times, knots were tied in ropes to govern;
後世易之以書契。」 hòushì yì zhī yǐ shūqì." later generations replaced them with written contracts."
先結繩， xiān jié shéng, First there were knotted ropes;
易化之效； yì huà zhī xiào; this was evidence of ease of transformation.
後書契， hòu shūqì, Later there were written contracts;
難治之驗也。 nán zhì zhī yàn yě. this was proof of the difficulty of governing.
故夫宓犧之前， gù fū Mìxī zhī qián, Therefore, before Fúxī,
The people were most simple and genuine.
Those who slept, rested comfortably;
those who sat, sat leisurely.
They lived in groups and gathered together,
knowing their mothers but not recognizing their fathers.
By the time of Fúxī,
the people had become somewhat refined,
knowing to use cunning to deceive the foolish,
the brave wanting to intimidate the timid,
the strong wanting to bully the weak,
the many wanting to tyrannize the few.
Therefore, Fúxī created the Eight Trigrams (bāguà) to govern them.
By the time of the Zhōu dynasty,
the people's refinement was shallow,
and the Eight Trigrams were difficult to reiterate and follow.
Therefore, King Wén expanded them into sixty-four hexagrams,
exhausting their permutations,
so that the people would not grow weary.
By the time of the Zhōu dynasty,
the people had long been shallow,
so Kǒngzǐ (Confucius) wrote the "Spring and Autumn Annals,"
selecting the slightest goodness,
denouncing the smallest evil,
saying:
"Zhōu (The Zhōu dynasty) observed the preceding two dynasties,
how rich and flourishing in culture!
I follow Zhōu."
Kǒngzǐ knew that the world was gradually deteriorating,
When culture is shallow, it is difficult to govern.
Therefore, (people) add layers of dense netting,
establishing extremely fine prohibitions,
employing checks and balances to maintain control,
with preparations complete and thorough.
These words are nonsense.
The people of ancient times
cherished the Five Constant Virtues;
the people of later times
also cherished the Five Constant Virtues.
Both cherish the Way of the Five Constant Virtues,
both are born receiving the same vital energy;
so how is it that ancient times were simple and unadorned?
How is it that later times are cultured and shallow?
Those people see that the people of ancient times
drank blood and ate fur,
without the food of the five grains.
Later generations dug wells into the earth,
cultivated the soil and planted grains,
drinking well water and eating millet,
with the tempering of water and fire;
they also see that in high antiquity, people lived in caves and nests,
wearing the skins of birds and beasts.
Later generations exchanged these for palaces and houses,
with adornments of cloth and silk.
Then they say that ancient times were simple and unadorned,
and later times were cultured and shallow.
夫 qì yè biàn yì,
while innate nature and conduct do not differ.
However, there are expressions like "simplicity" and "elegance,"
because the world experiences prosperity and decline.
Extreme decline inevitably leads to corruption.
shuāi jí jiǔ yǒu bì yě.
It is like clothing and food for people:
when first made, they are fresh and complete;
when first ripe, they are fragrant and clean;
after a short time, they are worn and torn;
after a few days, they are stinky and rotten.
The principles of elegance and substance
are shared by ancient and modern times.
One substance and one elegance,
one decline and one prosperity—
these existed in ancient times;
it's not unique to the present.
How can we verify this?
The *Commentary* says:
"The kings of the Xià Hòu Shì Dynasty taught with loyalty.
The superiors taught with loyalty,
and the gentlemen were loyal,
but the failing was that
the common people became unrefined.
To remedy unrefinedness, nothing is better than reverence.
The kings of the Yīn Dynasty taught with reverence.
The superiors taught with reverence,
and the gentlemen were reverent,
but the failing was that
the common people became superstitious.
To remedy superstition, nothing is better than elegance.
Therefore, the kings of the Zhōu Dynasty taught with elegance.
The superiors taught with elegance,
and gentlemen are refined,
the fault lies in that
the common person is unfeeling.
To remedy this unfeelingness, nothing is better than loyalty."
Those who succeed the Zhōu dynasty and become rulers,
should teach loyalty.
The Xià dynasty, which succeeded the teachings of Táng
and Yú, found them to be unfeeling,
therefore they taught loyalty.
If Táng and Yú taught refinement,
then those whom they succeeded must have lost their way in ghostliness.
When people see that refinement in the present day is unfeeling,
and they treat it with familiarity and scorn it,
they then say that the ancient world was simple and genuine,
and that the later world is refined and unfeeling,
it is like when family members are not careful,
one then says that the children of other families are careful and good.
The saying is that people of ancient times
valued righteousness and lightly regarded their own lives.
When they encountered matters of loyalty and righteousness,
and it was clear that they should give their lives,
則 bì fù tāng qū fēng, [then certainly they would rush into boiling water and towards sharp blades,]
sǐ bù gù hèn. [even dying without regard for resentment.]
Gù Hóng Yǎn zhī jié, [Therefore, the integrity of Hóng Yǎn,]
Chén Bùzhàn zhī yì, [the righteousness of Chén Bùzhàn,]
xíngshì bǐlèi, [examples of such actions, compared and classified,]
shūjí suǒ zài, [are recorded in books,]
wángmìng juān shēn, [sacrificing life and donating oneself,]
zhòngduō fēi yī. [are numerous, not just one.]
Jīnshì qū lì gǒu shēng, [Nowadays, people pursue profit and seek a wretched existence,]
qì yì wàng dé, [abandoning righteousness and recklessly seeking gain,]
bù xiāng miǎn yǐ yì, [not encouraging each other with righteousness,]
bù xiāng jī yǐ xíng, [nor spurring each other on with action,]
yì fèi shēn bù yǐ wéi lěi, [righteousness is abandoned, and they do not consider it a burden,]
xíng huī shì bù yǐ xiāng wèi. [action is ruined, and they do not fear each other.]
Cǐ yán wàng yě. [This is a reckless statement.]
Fú shàngshì zhī shì, [Now, the gentlemen of ancient times,]
jīnshì zhī shì yě, [and the gentlemen of today,]
jù hán rényì zhī xìng, [both possess the nature of benevolence and righteousness,]
zé qí zāo shì, [then, when they encounter affairs,]
bìng yǒu fèn shēn zhī jié. [they all have the integrity to devote themselves.]
Gǔ yǒu wúyì zhī rén, [In ancient times, there were unrighteous people,]
jīn yǒu jiàn jié zhī shì, [and today, there are gentlemen who establish integrity.]
Shàn'è zázè, [Good and evil are mixed,]
hé shì wú yǒu? [what age does not have them?]
Shùshì zhě hào gāo gǔ ér xià jīn, [Those who narrate affairs admire the high antiquity and disparage the present,]
guì suǒ wén ér jiàn suǒ jiàn. [value what they have heard and disdain what they have seen.]
Biàn shì zé tán qí jiǔ zhě, [Orators talk about what is old,]
Wénrén zé zhù qí yuǎn zhě. Literary men then record those who are distant (in time).

"Lěi Hài Piān" (Chapter on Accumulative Harm)
Generally, when people enter officialdom and are delayed and do not advance,

their sins accumulate and are not removed,
their reputation is obscured and not clear,
yet their talent is not inferior,
their conduct is not rebellious,
their knowledge is not muddled,
their strategies are not obscure,
but they encounter external calamities;
it is the accumulative harm that does it.
It is not only human actions
but all things are like this;
things that are living and moving
are all subject to accumulative harm.
Accumulative harm comes from the outside;
it does not originate from within.
Now, not understanding the origin of accumulative harm
And merely blaming those who are harmed

Things are born in the spring,

they mature in the autumn,

Suddenly, oxen and horses trample the roots,

Things that do not mature

A rat treads in cooked rice,

The flavor of the discarded rice

coming about not by my own doing

In general, a person's conduct

Shallow affection leads to resentment,

People's talents are high or low,

When advancing at the same time,
Those in high positions obtain honor,

Human interactions and friendships

Positions are few, people are many,

"Chapter on Fate and Fortune"
That ordinary people encounter chance and suffer burdens and harms
is all due to fate.
There is the fate of life and death, longevity and early demise,
and there is also the fate of nobility and lowliness, poverty and wealth.
From princes and dukes down to commoners,
sages and the most foolish,
all who have heads and eyes,
and belong to the blood-containing category,
none do not have fate.
If fate decrees poverty and lowliness,
even if one is enriched and ennobled,
they will still encounter misfortune and lose their wealth and nobility;
if fate decrees wealth and nobility,
even if one is impoverished and lowly,
they will still encounter good fortune and escape their poverty and lowliness.
Therefore, those with a noble fate
rise from humble beginnings,
while those with a lowly fate
are endangered from positions of wealth.
Thus, wealth and nobility seem to have divine assistance,
while poverty and lowliness seem to have ghostly misfortune.
People with a noble fate,
all learn and uniquely succeed,
and are uniquely promoted in official service;
people with a wealthy fate,
all seek and uniquely obtain,
and all uniquely achieve.
Poverty and lowliness are the opposite,
difficult to succeed, difficult to be promoted,
difficult to obtain, difficult to achieve;
To obtain past transgressions and receive punishment,
to have illness cause loss and abandonment,
to lose one's wealth and status,
is to be poor and lowly.
Therefore, to have high talent and profound conduct
does not necessarily guarantee one will be rich and noble.
To have little wisdom and thin virtue
is not necessarily to be believed to be poor and lowly.
Sometimes, to have high talent and profound conduct,
but a bad fate,
one is abandoned and does not advance.
To have little wisdom and thin virtue,
but a good fate,
one flourishes and surpasses.
Therefore, in facing matters, knowing foolishness,
conduct being clear or turbid,
is a matter of nature and talent.
Officialdom being noble or lowly,
managing property being poor or rich,
is a matter of fate and time.
Fate cannot be forced,
time cannot be influenced.
The wise attribute it to Heaven,
and therefore are broad-minded and indifferent,
even in their poverty and lowliness.
Making wealth and status like digging a ditch and chopping firewood,
adding an effort to strive,
To achieve a state of strength and vigor,
incessant digging will deepen the ditch,
and unceasing chopping will increase the firewood.
If even those without destiny
can all attain their desires,
how could there be worries of poverty, lowliness, misfortune, and danger?
However, it is possible that the ditch is not yet cleared but encounters a flood,
or the firewood is not yet abundant but encounters a tiger.
Not becoming a high official,
and not becoming wealthy through managing property
are like encountering a flood while digging a ditch
or encountering a tiger while chopping firewood.
Having talent but not being able to employ it,
having wisdom but not being able to implement it,
or employing it but not establishing success,
or implementing it but not accomplishing the task—
even with talent and wisdom like Kǒngzǐ,
there was still no accomplished success.
When people in the world see someone with high moral conduct,
they say:
"Such a worthy and wise person,
why isn't he noble?"
When they see someone with deep planning and consideration,
they say:
"Such a clever and insightful person,
why isn't he rich?"
Nobility and wealth are due to destiny, fortune, and prosperity;
It does not depend on the worthy, the wise, eloquence, or intelligence.
Therefore, it is said:
"Wealth cannot be obtained through calculation or strategy,
nor can nobility be achieved through talent and ability."
One may be deeply intelligent yet without wealth,
or possess great talent yet without official rank.
Wearing silver seals and purple ribbons [i.e., holding high office],
one may not possess the talent of Jì (稷) or Qì (契);
accumulating gold and piling up jade,
one may not possess the wisdom of Táo Zhū (陶朱).
Sometimes, the lowly and foolish amass a thousand gold pieces,
and the stubborn and dull govern cities.
Therefore, officials of the same talent
may have different destinies in terms of nobility;
those with similar knowledge in managing livelihoods
may have different fortunes in terms of wealth.
Fortune and destiny determine poverty and wealth;
knowledge cannot increase or decrease them.
Nature and destiny determine nobility and lowliness;
talent cannot advance or retreat them.
The talent of King Chéng (成王) was not as great as that of the Duke of Zhōu (周公);
the wisdom of Duke Huán (桓公) was not as good as that of Guǎn Zhòng (管仲),

Examining the ancients, rulers rarely failed to learn from their ministers,

while the minister, despite possessing great talent, still serves as a servant.
Therefore, nobility and lowliness are determined by fate,
not by intelligence or foolishness;
poverty and wealth depend on emolument,
not on stubbornness or cleverness.
Those who discuss affairs in the world believe that those with great talent should become generals and ministers,

The people of Yuè smoked him out of his cave,
so he could not escape,
and they forcibly installed him as their ruler.
And the mandate of Heaven is inevitable;
even if one tries to escape it,
one ultimately cannot depart from it.
Therefore, isn't it noble for a man not to seek but to attain it naturally?
"On Qi and Longevity"
Ordinary people's appointed fates are of two kinds:
first, the fate of what one is destined to encounter;
second, the fate of strength and weakness, longevity and premature death.
What one is destined to encounter
refers to death by weapons, burning, crushing, or drowning;
strength and longevity, weakness and premature death
refer to the thickness or thinness of the qi one is endowed with.
Death by weapons, burning, crushing, or drowning depends on the endowment one has as fate;
there is necessarily no fixed time for it.
As for strength and weakness, premature death and longevity, a hundred is taken as the standard;
those who do not reach a hundred
are naturally deficient in qi.
If the endowment of qi is thick, then the body is strong;
if the body is strong, then its lifespan is long;
if the qi is thin, then the body is weak;
if the body is weak, then its lifespan is short;
if the lifespan is short, then there are many illnesses
and short lifespans.
Dying shortly after birth,
or being injured before delivery,
is due to a thin and weak endowment;
people with a thick and strong endowment will certainly complete their allotted lifespan.
As for those who have no encounters,
live idly in impoverished conditions,
and die of shortness of breath,
this is because their endowment is thin
and they have exhausted its use.
To fully attain what one aspires to in one's heart is rare.
"Chapter on the Formless"
People receive primordial qi from Heaven,
each receiving a destiny of longevity or premature death,
to establish a long or short form,
just as potters use clay to make round sacrificial vessels (guǐ) and angled eaves (lián wǔ),
and metalworkers use copper to make trays (pán) and tubs (yú).
Once the shape of the vessel is formed,
it cannot be made smaller or larger;
once the human body is determined,
it cannot be decreased or increased.
Using qi as nature,
when nature is formed, destiny is set.
The body's qi and physical form embrace each other,
life and death depend on their appointed times.
Form cannot be changed,
destiny cannot be reduced or added to.
Speaking in terms of pottery and metalworking,
the length of human life
can be discussed.
Someone might object, saying:
When potters use clay to make round sacrificial vessels (guǐ) and angled eaves (lián wǔ),
once the round sacrificial vessels and angled eaves are formed,
they eventually break and are ruined,
and cannot be changed back.
But when metalworkers use copper to make trays (pán) and tubs (yú), even though the trays and tubs
have become vessels,
It can still be melted again,
a shallow dish can be made into a *zūn* vessel,
but a *zūn* vessel cannot be made into a *guǐ* vessel.
Humans receive their *qì* from Heaven,
and although each receives a destiny of lifespan and premature death,
establishing themselves with a physical form,
if they obtain good methods and divine medicines,
their form can be transformed,
and their lifespan can be increased.
Someone said:
When smelters transform and change things into vessels,
they must first use fire to burn and melt them,
then they can be made large, small, short, or long.
People hope to prolong their years,
and wish to be like bronze vessels,
they should have a transformation similar to a furnace and charcoal,
then their form will be changed;
if their form is changed,
their lifespan can also be increased.
How can people transform their form,
and be like bronze vessels melted by fire?
The *Lǐ* (Book of Rites) says:
"When floods descend,

Why?
Because when rainwater violently falls,

Separated from their original true forms, they become transient insects.
As ministers are cautious,

People desire transformation of their bodies,

Now, insects and snakes that haven't transformed,

Insects and snakes that haven't transformed,

transformed into fish and turtles,

Being eaten means their lifespan is shortened,

As time goes by,

People desire transformation of their bodies,

Even if the body doesn't transform,

Gōng of Lǔ, Niú Āi, was bedridden with illness,

Gǔn was executed on Yǔshān,
To transform into a yellow bear-like creature,

Moreover, the transformation of things follows the *qi*,

People constantly take medicine to solidify longevity,

Encountering temporal changes

Heaven and earth do not change,
the sun and moon do not alter,
the stars and planets do not disappear,

People receive proper *qi*,

At times men are transformed into women,
women are transformed into men,

changes because of the government,

When the Hàn dynasty rose,

Similarly, the essence of the Yellow River had a person

All creatures that wriggle and fly,

Born as an infant,
growing into a man,

from birth to death,

Those whose nature does not change,

As for the lifespan of those who change,

If people wish to change their form,

If one merely changes one's form, but one's lifespan doesn't increase,

The dragon, being a creature,

The nature of the dragon is such that

From this perspective,

how can Heaven endure increasing or decreasing a person's years?

The followers of Gāo Zōng, who increased it?

If you say the followers of Gāo Zōng
Only if the form and body change,

People receive qi from heaven,

When people are alive they can walk,

cannot be changed,

From life to old age,

The change of hair,

Among the things of the Five Elements,

Human nature,

tǔ dì zhī běn xìng yě.

shù jià fēng mào;

三軍之士，

*Ōuhuì Piān* ("Chapter on Coincidence")
Fate,
is the master of fortune and misfortune.

two coincidences and three confluences,

It was on behalf of two rulers that they emerged.

It happens of itself.

goodness and evil, right and wrong,

crime should be punished severely,

Chapter on Original Nature
Emotions and nature,
Are the foundation of human governance,
From which ritual and music arise.
Therefore, examining the extremes of emotions and nature,
Ritual is used as a preventative measure,
music is used as a means of restraint.
Because human nature contains humility, deference, and yielding,
ritual is created to fit its appropriateness;
because emotions contain likes, dislikes, joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure,
music is created to express reverence.
The means by which ritual controls,
and the reason music is created,
are emotion and nature.
In the past, scholars and former students

Shì Shuò of the Zhōu dynasty

"Essay on the Nature of Things"
Scholars of Confucianism argue:
"Heaven and earth intentionally produce humans."
This statement is absurd.
For heaven and earth combine their vital energies,
and humans are produced spontaneously;
just as husband and wife combine their vital energies,
and children are produced spontaneously.
Husband and wife combine their vital energies,
not because they intentionally want to produce a child at that moment,
but because their emotions and desires move them to unite,
and uniting results in the birth of a child.
Furthermore, husband and wife do not intentionally produce children,
which shows that heaven and earth do not intentionally produce humans.
Therefore, humans are born from heaven and earth,
like fish in a pool,
or lice on a person,
arising from vital energies,
and reproducing within their kind.
The myriad things born between heaven and earth,
are all one reality.
The Commentary says:
「Tiāndì bù gù shēng rén,
humans arose spontaneously by chance."
If that is so,
why do those who discuss matters say: "Heaven and earth are the furnace,
the myriad things are the copper,
yin and yang are the fire,
and creation is the craftsman"?
Now, the potter's use of fire
melts copper and bakes vessels,
that is why he does it;
but if you say, "Heaven and earth did not intentionally create humans,
humans arose spontaneously by chance,"
can it be said that the potter
does not intentionally make vessels,
but the vessels are formed spontaneously by chance?
If the analogy does not fit the matter,
it cannot be called an analogy;
if the writing does not match the reality,
it cannot be called correct.
He says:
This is an analogy for people receiving *qi*
that is not completely pure and uniform,
like the casting of copper results in different shapes,
and the firing of vessels depends on how they get the fire,
it is not saying that heaven and earth creating people
is the same as pottery.
In making analogies,
People all speak of human affairs.
Human affairs have an inherent structure,
which cannot be severed.
If you look at the head with your eyes,
the head cannot help but move;
if you join the hands with the feet,
the feet cannot help but sway.

If one considers a mansion to be a degree,
three degrees is also the sun's travel for three days,
in the time of one wave,
would it make the sun go back three days?
When Duke Sòng Jǐng sincerely
uttered three virtuous words,
Mars moved three mansions,
yet even those who discuss it say it is false.
Lord Lǔ Yáng, in contention,
disliked the sunset,
and with this one halberd wave,
without sincere or virtuous words,
the sun reversed for him,
is probably not true!
Furthermore, the sun is fire.
Even if a sage waved away fire,
they ultimately could not repel it.
When Lǔ Yáng Gōng waved at the sun,
how could he possibly make it go back?
Sometimes, during battle, the sun was exactly at mǎo (5-7 AM).
Because of the confusion of battle,
people thought the sun was setting.
They waved at it, turning left
on a curved path, and the sun seemed to go back.
The world loves the supernatural and strange,
and therefore they said it went back.
This is not what is meant.
The *Zhuàn Shū* (Commentary) says:
"Jīng Kē, for the Crown Prince of Yān,
plotted to assassinate the King of Qín,
and a white rainbow pierced the sun.
Master Wèi, for Qín,
planned the affair at Chángpíng,
and Venus eclipsed the Pleiades."
This says that profound sincerity moves Heaven,
and Heaven causes changes.
Now, to say that
"a white rainbow pierced the sun"
and "Venus eclipsed the Pleiades"
are real.
Speaking of Jīng Kē's 荊軻 plan and
Wèi Xiānshēng's 衛先生 strategy,
to say they moved the heavens
such that a white rainbow pierced the sun and
Venus eclipsed the Pleiades is
false.
If you strike a bell with chopsticks,
or beat a drum with counting rods,
it won't make a sound,
because what you use to strike
is too small.
Now, a person's form is no more than seven *chǐ* (feet),
and with this seven *chǐ* form, focusing one's spirit
to try to accomplish something,
even if accumulating intense intention,
is like striking a bell with chopsticks or beating a drum with counting rods.
How can it move the heavens?
It's not that the spirit is insincere,
but that what's used to move (heaven) is too small.
Moreover, what one wants to harm is a person;
if the person isn't moved,
how could the heavens be moved instead?
Someone asks:
"Can a person's harmful energy
move each other?"
I reply:
"It cannot."
"Yù Ràng 豫讓 wanted to harm Zhào Xiāngzǐ 趙襄子,
and Xiāngzǐ's 襄子 heart was moved.
Guàn Gāo 貫高 wanted to usurp power from Gāo Zǔ 高祖,
and Gāo Zǔ's 高祖 heart was also moved.
These two men harbored intense spirit,
and therefore both rulers trembled."
It is said:
When calamity is about to arrive,
the body itself already possesses strangeness;
this is not something that ordinary people can influence.
How can this be verified?
Sometimes one encounters a madman on the road,
who wields a blade against oneself;
the madman may not necessarily intend to harm one's person,
yet one's body has already exhibited omens beforehand.
From this, it can be said that
the arrival of omens
is a sign that calamity is impending,
and is not caused by those who intend to harm oneself.
Moreover, a person marked by misfortune who receives an inauspicious divination,
obtains a bad hexagram through casting lots,
sees something unlucky upon exiting the door,
and perceives an aura of calamity through divination.
The aura of calamity appears on the face,
just as white rainbows and Venus appear in the sky.
Changes manifest in the sky,
and omens emerge from people;
the above and below spontaneously,
correspond to each other.
The *Commentary* says:
"Yān Tàizǐ Dān 燕太子丹 paid court to Qin,
but was not allowed to leave.
He requested permission from the King of Qin to return.
The King of Qín held him back
and made an oath with him, saying:
'If the sun rises in the middle of the day again,
if the sky rains millet,
if the crows turn white-headed,
if horses grow horns,
and if the wooden image on the kitchen door grows flesh feet,
then you may return.'
At that time,
Heaven aided him,
and the sun rose in the middle of the day again,
the sky rained millet,
the crows turned white-headed,
horses grew horns,
and the wooden image on the kitchen door grew flesh feet.
The King of Qín considered it a miracle
and allowed him to return."
This saying is false.
What kind of person was Yān Tàizǐ Dān 燕太子丹?
How could he move Heaven?
Even when a sage is imprisoned,
cannot move Heaven.
Tàizǐ Dān, a worthy man,
how could he bring this about?
If Heaven could bless the Prince,
causing auspicious signs to arise and thus deliver him,
then it could harmonize with the Qín King's intentions, thereby resolving his difficulties.
Securing one easy thing is easy,
but producing five auspicious signs is difficult.
To abandon the easy task of one thing,
in favor of the difficult task of five things,
why would Heaven not fear the effort?
Tāng was trapped in the Xià Terrace,
Wén Wáng was imprisoned in Yǒulǐ,
Kǒngzǐ was beset in Chén and Cài.
The troubles of these three sages,
Heaven could not help,
to make those who confined them see the blessings and know their sanctity,
and release them to be honored.
Someone might say:
"Those who confined the three sages did not make a vow to them,
the hearts of the three sages were unwilling,
therefore, the auspicious signs blessing the sages had no reason to appear.
Heaven's blessing of people
is like lending people objects or tools;
if people do not seek or request them,
then they will not be given."
I say:
When the Prince desired auspicious signs throughout the land,
豈有語言乎？ [Qǐ yǒu yǔyán hū?] Could there be language (to describe it)?
心願而已。 [Xīnyuàn éryǐ.] It is only a matter of the heart's desires.
然 Tāng 閉於夏臺、 [Rán Tāng bì yú Xiàtái,] However, when Tāng was imprisoned in the Terrace of Xià,
文王拘於羑里時， [Wén Wáng jū yú Yǒulǐ shí,] and King Wén was detained in Yǒulǐ,
心亦願出； [xīn yì yuàn chū;] their hearts also desired to be released;
孔子厄陳、蔡， [Kǒngzǐ è Chén, Cài,] when Kǒngzǐ was in distress in Chén and Cài,
心願食。 [xīn yuàn shí.] his heart desired food.
天何不令夏臺、羑里關鑰毀敗， [Tiān hé bù lìng Xiàtái, Yǒulǐ guānyào huǐbài,] Why did Heaven not cause the locks and keys of the Terrace of Xià and Yǒulǐ to be destroyed and broken,
湯、文涉出； [Tāng, Wén shè chū;] so that Tāng and King Wén could escape?
雨粟陳、蔡， [Yǔ sù Chén, Cài,] Why did it not rain millet in Chén and Cài,
孔子食飽乎？ [Kǒngzǐ shí bǎo hū?] so that Kǒngzǐ could eat his fill?
太史公曰： [Tàishǐgōng yuē:] The Grand Historian said:
「世稱太子丹之令 [Shì chēng Tàizǐ Dān zhī lìng] "The world claims that the order of Crown Prince Dān
天雨粟，馬生角， [tiān yǔ sù, mǎ shēng jiǎo,] caused Heaven to rain millet and horses to grow horns;
大抵皆虛言也。」 [dàdǐ jiē xūyán yě."] for the most part, these are all false statements."
太史公、書漢世實事之人， [Tàishǐgōng, shū Hàn shì shíshì zhī rén,] The Grand Historian, a person who recorded true events of the Hàn dynasty,
而云「虛言」， [ér yún "xūyán",] and yet he says "false statements";
近非實也。 [jìn fēi shí yě.] this is likely not true.
《傳書》言： [《Chuánshū》 yán:] The *Chuánshū* (a lost commentary on the *Shījīng*) says:
「杞梁氏之妻嚮城而哭， [“Qǐ Liángshì zhī qī xiàng chéng ér kū,] "The wife of Qǐ Liángshì faced the city and wept,
城為之崩。」 [chéng wèi zhī bēng."] and the city walls collapsed for her."
此言杞梁 [Cǐ yán Qǐ Liáng] This says that Qǐ Liáng
從軍不還， [cóngjūn bù hái,] went to war and did not return,
其妻痛之， [qí qī tòng zhī,] his wife grieved for him,
嚮城而哭， [xiàng chéng ér kū,] faced the city and wept,
至誠悲痛， [zhìchéng bēitòng,] with utmost sincerity and sorrow,
精氣動城， [jīngqì dòng chéng,] her vital essence moved the city,
故城為之崩也。 [gù chéng wèi zhī bēng yě.] therefore, the city walls collapsed for her.
夫言嚮城而哭者， [Fú yán xiàng chéng ér kū zhě,] Now, saying that she faced the city and wept,
實也； [shí yě;] is true;
言城為之崩者， [yán chéng wèi zhī bēng zhě,] saying that the city walls collapsed for her,
虛也。 [xū yě.] is false.
Of those who cry from grief, none surpasses Yōngmén Zǐ.
Yōngmén Zǐ cried in response to Mèngcháng Jūn,
and Mèngcháng Jūn felt sorrow for him in the city.
Indeed, the sincerity of the weeping
is why those who responded to it felt distressed and deeply moved.
Yōngmén Zǐ could move the heart of Mèngcháng,
but could not move the clothing of Mèngcháng,
because clothing does not know empathy
and does not connect with human feelings.
Now, city walls are made of earth,
and earth is like clothing;
it has no inner feelings.
How could it collapse from sorrow and deep emotion caused by weeping?
If the sound of utter sincerity could move city walls,
then if one cried towards forests and trees,
could they break grass and shatter wood?
If one wept towards water and fire,
could they cause water to gush forth or extinguish fire?
Grass, trees, water, and fire are no different from earth;
yet Qǐliáng's wife could not collapse the city walls,
which is clear.
Perhaps the city walls happened to collapse on their own,
and Qǐliáng's wife happened to be crying;
later generations love falsehood,
not seeking the truth of the matter.
Therefore, the reputation of collapsing the city walls
has not been extinguished to this day.
The *Traditionary Book* says:
"Zōu Yǎn was innocent,
but was imprisoned in Yān.
In the fifth month of summer,
he looked up to the sky and sighed,
and the heavens caused frost to fall."
This is no different from Qǐ Liáng's wife weeping and the city wall collapsing.
There is no difference.
The statement that he was innocently imprisoned
and sighed to the heavens in summer is a fact;
it is real.
The statement that the heavens caused frost to fall for him
is false; it is not real.
Even if ten thousand people raised their voices and all expressed sighs of grief,
they still would not be able to move Heaven.
How could Zōu Yǎn, alone, unjustly wronged, with but one sigh,
cause frost to fall?
Zōu Yǎn's injustice
was no more than that of Zēng Zǐ and Bó Qí.
Zēng Zǐ was doubted and chanted,
Bó Qí was expelled and sang.
Doubt, expulsion, and imprisonment are the same,
chanting, singing, and sighing are equivalent,
Zēng Zǐ and Bó Qí could not bring about cold,
Zōu Yǎn, what kind of person was he,
that he alone could make it rain frost?
The injustice of being expelled
is still not enough to speak of.
Shēn Shēng submitted to the sword,
Zǐ Xū cut his own throat,
were truly filial but were given death,
were truly loyal but were executed,
and moreover, at the time of death, both had vocal utterances.
These utterances, once spoken,
were no different from sighing to the heavens,
but the heavens were not moved for these two men,
only for Zōu Yǎn were they moved,
could it be that heaven is pained to see imprisonment,
but not saddened by bloodshed?
Bó Qí's grievance and pain were similar,
but the moving of heaven was different?
Now, to dry with a single torch, to heat with a single cauldron of water,
it will not become hot all day;
to lean on a one-foot ice block, to place it in the kitchen,
it will not become cold all night.
Why is this?
Small sensations cannot move great things.
Now, Zōu Yǎn's 鄒衍 sigh,
is nothing more than like a torch or a foot of ice,
while the majestic heavens are vast,
not merely the ugly things in a cauldron or kitchen.
If one looks up to the sky and sighs,
the heavens cause frost to fall,
why are the heavens so easily moved,
and the frost so easily brought down?
Alas, sorrow and joy are the same,
happiness and anger are equal.
Yǎn 衍 raised resentment and pain,
causing frost to descend on the world,
causing Yǎn 衍 to receive unwarranted rewards.
If he looks up to the sky and laughs,
can he, in the winter season, make the heavens warm?
The school of "change and return" says:
"If the ruler bestows rewards in autumn, then it becomes warm,
if he inflicts punishments in summer, then it becomes cold."
If cold does not accumulate, then frost will not fall;
if warmth does not last for days, then ice will not melt.
If one man is wronged and sighs once,
the heavens immediately send down frost,
why are the atmospheric conditions so easily changed,
and the seasons so easily reversed?
Cold and warmth each have their own time,
which does not accord with the sayings of the school of "change and return."
Moreover, according to the theory of "change and return,"
perhaps the King of Yān 燕 was fond of using punishments at that time,
Cold air should arrive;
and Yǎn was imprisoned and sighed,
as he sighed, frost just then descended.
The world saw that as he sighed, frost descended,
and therefore said that Zōu Yǎn's sigh caused it.
The *Chuánshū* says:
"Shī Kuàng played the tune of 《Báixuě》 (White Snow),
and divine beings descended because of it,
wind and rain violently arrived,
Duke Píng suffered from illness because of it,
the state of Jìn became red earth."
Some say: "Shī Kuàng's tune of 《Qīngjiǎo》 (Clear Horn),
once played,
clouds rose from the northwest;
played again,
a great wind arrived,
heavy rain followed,
tearing the curtains,
breaking the sacrificial vessels,
and dislodging the tiles from the corridors.
Those seated scattered and fled,
Duke Píng was fearful,
hiding in a side room of the corridor.
The state of Jìn suffered a great drought,
red earth for three years,
Duke Píng suffered from illness."
Now, 《Báixuě》 and 《Qīngjiǎo》,
are perhaps the same tune with different names,
their calamities and failures are essentially the same.
The families who transmit the *Chuánshū*,
record it as true;
the common people observing,
and believe it to be so.
Examining the actual truth,
[it] is likely empty words.
Now, what kind of sound is "Qīng Jiǎo"
that it can cause this?
[They] say:
"'Qīng Jiǎo' is a wood sound,
therefore it causes wind and rain.
Like wood creating wind,
rain and wind come together."
Three feet of wood,
the sound of several strings,
moving heaven and earth,
how miraculous is that?
This is just like one cry collapsing a city,
one sigh causing frost to fall, and such things.
Shī Kuàng was able to play "Qīng Jiǎo,"
he must have received instruction,
he wasn't able to naturally produce it.
When he first received instruction,
he practiced day and night,
not just playing it once or twice.
If we thoroughly examine the words in the *Zhuàn Shū*,
when Shī Kuàng learned "Qīng Jiǎo",
wind and rain should have arrived then.
The "Record of Transmissions" says:
"When Hù Bā played the zither,
the fish in the deep came out to listen;
when Shī Kuàng played the qin,
the six horses raised their heads and ate no more."
Some say:
"When Shī Kuàng played "Qīngjiǎo,"
at the first performance,
there were sixteen black cranes, coming from the south,
gathering on the high part of the gate porch;
at the second performance, they lined up;
at the third performance,
they stretched their necks and cried,
spread their wings and danced,
their sound matched the *gōng* and *shāng* tones,
their cries echoed to the heavens.
Lord Píng was greatly pleased,
and all who were present rejoiced."
The *Book of Documents* says:
"Strike the stones, pat the stones,
and all the beasts will dance."
Although this is strange and wonderful,
it is still believable.
Why is that?
Birds and beasts love mournful sounds,
and their ears are the same as human ears.
When birds and beasts see that people want to eat,
they also want to eat them,
When they hear human joy,
why wouldn't they also be joyful?
However, the stories of "fish listening," "horses grazing upwards," "black cranes stretching their necks," and "all beasts dancing together"
are probably true to some extent.
But the stories of wind and rain arriving, the state of Jìn 晉 experiencing a great drought,
the land being red for three years, and Píng Gōng 平公 suffering from paralysis
are likely fabrications.
Perhaps when the *Qīng Jiǎo* 清角 melody was played,
there happened to be wind and rain,
and after the wind and rain,
the state of Jìn 晉 coincidentally experienced a drought.
Píng Gōng 平公 loved music
and laughed excessively,
and coincidentally developed paralysis.
The families who transmit these stories
believed them to be true,
and when people in the world saw them,
they came to regard them as facts.
In reality, the music cannot bring about such things.
How can we verify this?
Violent wind and rain storms
This is the disorder of *yin* and *yang*.
If music can disrupt *yin* and *yang*,
then it can also regulate *yin* and *yang*.
What need then for a ruler to cultivate himself and rectify his conduct,
and broadly implement benevolent policies?
Just have the drums play tunes that regulate *yin* and *yang*,
and harmonious *qi* will arrive naturally,
and peace will establish itself.
The *Commentary to the Book [of Documents]* says:
"Tāng encountered a seven-year drought,
and prayed with his body in Sānglín,
blaming himself for six faults,
and then heaven rained."
Some say: "Five years.
The prayer said:
'If I, the one man, am guilty,
let it not extend to the myriad people;
if the myriad people are guilty,
let it rest on me, the one man.
Heaven must not, because of the lack of diligence of one man,
cause God and the spirits to harm the lives of the people.'
Thereupon he cut his hair,
bound his hands,
and regarded himself as a sacrificial animal,
to pray for blessings to God.
God was greatly pleased,
and timely rain then arrived."
If we say that Tāng prayed in the Mulberry Forest, blaming himself,
like saying he cut his hair and adorned his hands,
considering himself a sacrificial offering,
to pray for blessings from the Supreme Deity,
then that is true.
But to say that the rain came
because Tāng blamed himself and prayed with his body,
that is probably a fabrication.
When Kǒngzǐ fell ill,
Zǐlù asked to offer prayers.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Is there such a thing?"
Zǐlù said:
"Yes, there is;
the *Lěi* [Funeral Oration] says:
'Pray to you, the gods above and below.'"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Qiū's prayers have been for a long time."
The sage cultivates his person and rectifies his conduct;
his customary prayers have been for a long time.
Heaven and earth, spirits and gods,
know that he is without guilt,
therefore he said, "Prayed for a long time."
The *Yì* [Book of Changes] says:
"The great person unites his virtue with Heaven and Earth,
unites his brightness with the sun and moon,
unites his order with the four seasons,
"To unite with the spirits in their auspiciousness and misfortune."
This speaks of the sage being of the same virtue and conduct as Heaven and Earth and the spirits.
That one must pray to obtain blessings
indicates that they are not the same.
Tāng and Kǒngzǐ were both sages,
both of whom prayed regularly for a long time.
Kǒngzǐ did not have Zǐlù pray to cure illness,
so how could Tāng obtain rain through prayer?
Kǒngzǐ prayed regularly,
yet he still suffered from illness;
Tāng also prayed regularly,
yet the year still experienced a great drought.
Thus, Heaven and Earth having floods and droughts
is like people having illnesses.
Illnesses cannot be removed by self-reproach,
and floods and droughts cannot be dispelled by prayers of apology;
this is clear.
Did Tāng cause the drought
due to some transgression?
That would mean he is not of the same virtue as Heaven and Earth.
If it wasn't caused by transgression,
then self-reproach and prayers of apology
are also of no benefit.
A human form is seven feet tall,
within the form are the five constant virtues,
and one can have a feverish illness.
Even with deep self-reproach,
one still cannot be cured.
How much more so with the vastness of Heaven,
which has its own changes of floods and droughts?
How can Tāng, using his seven-foot form,
and the sincerity within that form,
remove the drought through self-reproach and prayers of apology?
How could he possibly obtain rain?
A person is on top of a layered terrace,
and people bow their heads beneath the layered terrace,
requesting things from the person on the terrace.
The person on the terrace hears their words,
and then pities them and gives to them;
but if they do not hear their words,
even if they are utterly sincere,
in the end they will obtain nothing.
Now, the distance between Heaven and man,
is not just the height of a layered terrace.
Although Tāng blamed himself,
how could Heaven hear and know and give him rain?
Now, drought is a transformation of fire;
and inundation is a change of water.
Yáo encountered a great flood,
which could be called inundation.
Yáo did not blame himself and use his body to pray,
but necessarily had Shùn and Yǔ control it,
knowing that a water transformation must be controlled.
Eliminating inundation is not done through prayer,
eliminating drought should also be like that.
From this perspective,
Tāng's 湯 prayers could not bring rain.
Sometimes, after a long drought,
the time is right for rain to fall on its own.
Tāng 湯, because of the long drought,
happened to blame himself as well.
People saw the rain fall
following Tāng's 湯 self-blame,
and therefore said that Tāng 湯 obtained rain through prayer.
The *Zhuàn Shū* 傳書 states:
"Cāng Jié 倉頡 made writing,
and the sky rained millet,
and ghosts cried at night."
This means that when literature flourished, disorder gradually appeared,
so the strange phenomena
resulted in the sky raining millet and ghosts crying at night.
Speaking of the sky raining millet and ghosts crying at night,
is a reality.
Saying that it was in response to Cāng Jié's 倉頡 creation of writing,
is false.
Now, the Yellow River produced the *Diagram* (Tú 圖),
and the Luo River produced the *Document* (Shū 書),
these are auspicious responses to sagely emperors and enlightened kings.
The Diagrams and Documents, the writings, how are they different from the writings made by Cāng Jié 倉頡?
Tiāndì wèi túshū, The universe serves as books,
Cāngjié zuò wénzì, Cāngjié created writing,
Yè yǔ tiāndì tóng, His work is the same as that of the universe,
Zhǐ yǔ guǐshén hé, His intent aligns with spirits and deities,
Hé fēi hé è, What is wrong or evil,
Ér zhì yǔ sù, shén kū zhī guài zāi? That it would cause the strange phenomena of rain of millet and weeping spirits?
Shǐ tiāndì guǐshén è rén yǒu shū, If the universe, spirits, and deities hate humans possessing writing,
Zé qí chū túshū Then their production of the universe as books
fēi yě; is wrong;
tiān bù è rén yǒu shū, If the universe does not hate humans possessing writing,
zuò shū hé fēi, ér zhì cǐ guài? What is wrong with creating writing, that it would cause this strangeness?
Huò shí Cāngjié shì zuò shū, Perhaps Cāngjié happened to be creating writing,
tiān shì yǔ sù, The universe happened to rain millet,
guǐ ǒu yè kū, And spirits happened to weep at night,
ér yǔ sù, And the rain of millet,
guǐshén kū, And the weeping of spirits and deities,
zì yǒu suǒ wéi, each had their own reasons,
shì jiàn yìng shū ér zhì, But the world sees them as happening in response to the writing,
zé wèi zuò shū shēng luàn bài zhī xiàng, And thus says that the creation of writing produces omens of chaos and failure,
yìng shì ér dòng yě. And that it responds to events and acts accordingly.
"Tiān yǔ gǔ," "The universe rains grain,"
lùn zhě wèi zhī cóng tiān ér xià, Commentators say it comes from above,
yìng biàn ér shēng. Born in response to change.
Rú yǐ yúnyǔ lùn zhī, If we discuss it in terms of clouds and rain,
yǔ gǔ zhī biàn, The strangeness of the rain of grain,
bùzú guài yě. is not worth wondering at.
How can this be verified?
Now, clouds and rain originate from hills and mountains,
and when they descend and disperse, they become rain.
People see it falling from above,
and so they call it "heaven rains water."
In summer days, it rains water,
in winter days, the weather is cold, so the rain congeals and becomes snow,
all of which originate from the cloud vapor rising from the hills and mountains,
not descending and gathering from the sky onto the earth,
this is clear.
Now, the "rain" of grain
is also because cloud spreads out
and rises from the earth,
consequently blowing together with strong winds,
mixing in the sky,
and gathering on the earth.
People see it falling from the sky,
and so they call it "heaven rains grain."
During the 31st year of the Jiànwǔ reign (of Emperor Guāngwǔ of the Eastern Hàn),
in Chénliú, it rained grain,
and the fallen grain covered the ground.
Upon examining the shape of the grain,
it was like thatch and black,
resembling barnyard millet seeds.
Perhaps at that time, in the land of the Eastern Īdí barbarians,
this grain grew,
but the Īdí barbarians do not eat grains,
so this grain grows in the wilderness,
ripens, and hangs withered to the ground,
then encounters a sudden strong wind,
which blows it up, and it flies along with the wind,
when the wind weakens, the grain gathers and falls onto Zhōngguó (Central China).
Zhōngguó people see it,
and calls it "heaven-rained grain."
How is this like?
A wildfire burns mountains and marshes.
Within the mountains and marshes,
grasses and trees are all burned.
Their leaves become ash.
A sudden violent wind arises,
blows them up,
and they fly up to the sky.
When the wind weakens, the leaves fall down,
gathering on the roads.
The so-called "heaven-rained grain"
is similar to the burnt leaves of grasses and trees flying and gathering.
Yet the world thinks it is rained grain,
and those who write *Chuán Shū* (Commentaries and Records) consider it a strange phenomenon.
Heaven is responsible for dispensing *qì* (vital energy),
and earth is responsible for producing things.
Whatever leaves and fruits can be pecked and eaten
are all produced by the earth,
not done by heaven.
Now, grain is not produced by *qì*.
It requires earth to be formed.
Though it speaks of strange transformations,
strange transformations are based on categories.
Things that are born from the earth
further gather from the heavens.
Things born of the heavens,
can they come from the earth?
The earth's possession of myriad things
is like the heavens' possession of the arrayed stars.
The stars do not newly grow from the earth,
so why should grain alone grow from the heavens?
The *Commentary Book* also says:
"Bó Yì made a well,
dragons ascended to the dark clouds,
spirits dwelled on Kūnlún."
It says that the dragon well was harmful,
therefore the dragons and spirits transformed.
Now, the statement that dragons ascended to the dark clouds
is fact.
The statement that spirits dwelled on Kūnlún,
and further stating it was because of the well making,
that the dragons ascended and the spirits departed,
is fiction.
Now, making wells and drinking
and tilling fields and eating
are both equally factual.
Bó Yì made wells,
resulting in changes.
From the beginning for those who plow and weed,
why are there no changes?
Shénnóng fashioned a curved wood into a plow,
teaching the people to plow and weed,
the people began to eat grains,
grains began to be sown.
Plowing the soil to make fields,
digging the ground to make wells,
wells produce water to relieve thirst,
fields produce grain to relieve hunger,
this is what heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits desire to do,
why does the dragon ascend the dark clouds?
Why do the gods reside in Kūnlún?
That the dragon ascends the dark clouds,
has existed from ancient times to the present,
it is not that only after Yì made wells that it ascended.
Now it is high summer,
thunder and rain arrive at the proper time,
dragons often ascend the clouds.
Clouds and rain correspond with dragons,
dragons ride on clouds and rain to travel,
things of a kind attract each other,
it is not purposeful.
In Yáo's time,
the world was greatly harmonious,
The people had nothing to do.
There were people, around fifty in number, playing the game of hitting the earth with clods on the road.
Onlookers said:
"How great is the virtue of Yáo!"
The one hitting the clods said:
"I rise at sunrise to work,
and rest at sunset.
I dig a well to drink,
and cultivate the fields to eat.
What power does Yáo have?"
Wells already existed in the time of Yáo.
During the time of the Táng and Yú dynasties,
there were those who raised dragons and those who controlled dragons.
Dragons were always at court.
At the end of the Xià dynasty, when governance declined,
the dragons then went into hiding.
It wasn't because Yì dug wells
that the dragons ascended into the clouds.
What is meant by "divinity"?
What kind of divinity is it?
All the gods are like this;
why would all the gods hate people for digging wells?
If the gods are the same as people,
then they should also have the desire to drink.
If they have the desire to drink,
hating the well and leaving would
not be the truth.
Yì almost certainly did not dig wells;
dragons do not ascend to the clouds for the sake of well-digging;
spirits do not dwell on Kūnlún;
the writings transmitted are intentionally misleading,
intended to deceive future generations.
The *Zhuàn Shū* says:
"Liáng Shān collapsed,
damming the river, preventing it from flowing for three days,
and the Jìn ruler worried about it.
Jìn Bózōng, based on the words of a cart driver,
ordered Jǐng Gōng to wear plain white mourning clothes and weep,
and the river flowed again."
This is a false statement.
The collapse of a mountain damming a river
is like a person having a carbuncle or tumor,
with blood vessels blocked.
Can one treat a carbuncle or tumor
by wearing plain clothes and weeping?
In the time of Yáo,
the great flood reached the sky,
engulfing mountains and flooding hills.
Emperor Yáo sighed and lamented,
widely seeking wise men.
The flood was worse than the river being dammed,
Yáo's worries were deeper than Jǐng Gōng's,
I have not heard that the sound of weeping in plain white silk
can overcome it.
Did Yáo not have the skill of a cart driver?
Even if the flood became great,
could it not be subdued and removed by sound?
Just as "weeping in plain white silk"
is regretting mistakes and blaming oneself,
Yáo and Yǔ's control of the floods was through physical labor,
not self-blame.
Mount Liáng,
was Mount Yáo's time;
the blocked river,
was the river in Yáo's time.
The mountain collapses and the river is blocked,
heaven rains and water surges,
the changes in these two are not different.
Yáo and Yǔ controlled the floods with physical labor,
the cart driver controlled the blocked river by blaming himself,
the changes are the same but the control is different,
people are equal but the responses are different,
it is probably not the essence of sages and their transformative recovery.
Generally speaking, the principle of transformative recovery,
that which can move each other,
is based on the category of things.
When there is cold, restore it with warmth,
warmth can be relieved with cold.
Therefore, using dragons to bring rain,
and using punishments to drive away heat,
are all based on the qi of the Five Elements,
using them to mutually influence and overcome each other.
If a mountain collapses and blocks a river,
to wear white mourning clothes and weep for it,
what meaning is there in this principle?
Perhaps this was when the river was blocked,
and the mountain had just collapsed,
the earth had accumulated,
and the water had not yet surged.
After three days,
the water surged, the earth scattered, gradually breaking down and crumbling.
As it broke down and crumbled, the water flowed,
finally flowing eastward.
They encountered the words of someone who obtained the carriage of Bó Zōng,
and because of the white mourning clothes, they wept,
they wept because of the flow,
and when it flowed, they said the river's change started from this and recovered.
But in reality, it is not so.
How to verify this?
If the mountain were to constantly collapse by itself?
Wearing white mourning clothes and weeping would be of no benefit.
If it is a heavenly change that responds to it,
one should change the governance.
Wearing white mourning clothes and weeping,
what governance is being changed, so that the heavenly change would be reversed?
The "Commentary on the Book of Documents" says:
"Zēngzǐ's 曾子 filial piety
was such that he shared the same vital energy (qì) with his mother.
Zēngzǐ 曾子 went to the fields to gather firewood.
A guest arrived and wanted to leave.
Zēngmǔ 曾母 said:
'I wish to keep him here;
Shēn 參 will arrive soon.'
And she immediately used her right hand to squeeze her left arm.
Zēngzǐ's 曾子 left arm immediately felt pain.
He immediately rushed back, and asked his mother
saying: 'Why does my arm hurt?'
His mother said:
'Just now, a guest came and wanted to leave,
so I squeezed my arm to call you back.'
This is because, with utmost filial piety,
he shared the same vital energy with his parents;
if their bodies had an illness,
his spirit would immediately sense it."
Someone said:
"This is false."
The saying, "The utmost of filial piety and fraternal love
reaches the spirits and deities,"
means that virtuous transformation reaches Heaven and Earth.
Vulgar people, following this line of reasoning, say,
that in the utmost state of filial piety and fraternal love,
essence and vital energy interact.
If Zēng Mǔ's arm ached,
Zēng Zǐ's arm would also ache.
If Zēng Mǔ was sick, would Zēng Zǐ also be sick?
If Zēng Mǔ died,
would Zēng Zǐ also die?
Examining the matter,
Zēng Mǔ died first,
and Zēng Zǐ did not die.
This shows that vital essence can slightly affect each other,
but cannot greatly influence each other.
People say that Shēn Xǐ heard his mother singing at night,
and his heart was moved.
He opened the gate and asked who was singing,
and it was indeed his mother.
Because he heard his mother's voice,
voices can affect each other,
his heart was saddened and his intentions stirred.
He opened the gate and asked,
which was the real reason.
Now, if Zēng Mǔ is at home,
and Zēng Zǐ is in the field,
and he doesn't hear the sound of her calling,
how can his mother slightly pinching her arm,
possibly affect her son?
I suspect that people are praising and embellishing,
having heard that Zēng Zǐ's filial piety is unmatched in the world,
and thus fabricated the story of the mother pinching her arm.
It is commonly said:
Zhuó Gōng of Nányáng, when serving as magistrate of Gōushì,
locusts did not enter his boundary.
The reason given is that, due to his virtuousness and utmost sincerity,
calamitous insects did not enter his county.
This is again a fallacy.
The transformative power of virtuousness and utmost sincerity
communicates with those of the same kind,
enabling mutual understanding,
and then admiration and submission.
Locusts and
horseflies are of a different category.
How could they know or perceive and be aware of Zhuó Gōng's transformative influence?
If a virtuous person were to live deep in the wilderness,
would horseflies not enter their dwelling?
If horseflies cannot avoid the dwelling of a virtuous person,
how could locusts not enter Zhuó Gōng's county?
If one were to say that locusts are different and distinct from horseflies,
then cold and heat are also calamitous changes.
If an entire commandery is cold,
and a virtuous person governs one county within it,
could the boundary of that one county alone be warm?
If cold and heat cannot avoid the county of a virtuous person,
how could locusts not enter Zhuó Gōng's boundary?
Therefore,
If locusts happened not to enter the border,
and if Zhuō Gōng's reputation for virtue was occasionally praised in the world,
the world would then say he was able to ward off locusts.
How can this be verified?
When locusts gather in the fields,
they cannot universally and broadly cover all the land;
they often accumulate in large or small quantities in certain places.
The land where they do not accumulate,
is perhaps where Dào Zhí resided;
the fields where they are scarce,
is perhaps where Bó Yí lived.
Passing through, accumulating in large or small quantities,
cannot completely cover everything.
The amount of land they accumulate on,
means that passing through the county there will be some that leave or remain.
Quantity
cannot be used to verify good or evil,
presence or absence
how can it clarify virtue and wickedness?
It is simply that the locusts passed by of their own accord,
it is not because a virtuous person's border was not entered, this is clear.
"The Empty Fortune Chapter"

people act,

to show that virtue is rewarded;

There was a man of Sòng who liked to do good deeds,

because it can be drawn,

He argued:

He said:

Ghosts are called spirits,

says that Léi (雷)
Heaven's anger is roaring and sighing;
the "Diagram of Thunder" school,

The *Lǐ* (Book of Rites) says:

One goes out and one goes in,

The shape of the engaging pivots,

This is an imitation of its kind.
When the qi mutually engages as pivots and splits apart,

is the sound of engaging pivots.
The sound of a sudden, tearing rip,

If the qi shoots and hits a person,

The truthful explanation
of thunder is that it is the excited qi of the sun.
How is this made clear?
In the first month, *yáng* moves,
therefore thunder begins in the first month.
In the fifth month, *yáng* is at its peak,
therefore thunder is rapid in the fifth month.
In autumn and winter, *yáng* declines,
therefore thunder lies dormant in autumn and winter.
During the height of summer,
the sun is in charge,
and *yīn qì* invades it.
When Yīnyáng separate and contend,
they then mutually clash and rub.
Clashing and rubbing then causes spurting forth.
Spurting forth creates poison.
If it hits a person, they immediately die.
If it hits a tree, the tree breaks.
If it hits a house, the house collapses.
If a person is under a tree or between houses,

How can this be verified?
Try pouring a *dǒu* of water onto fire used for smelting and casting.
The vapor violently bursts apart,

If one is close to it,

Heaven and earth act as a furnace, how vast!
Yángqì acts as fire, how fierce!

If separation and contention spurts forth,

If it hits and wounds a person's body,

When smelting workers melt iron,

If it is dry, the iron goes down smoothly.

If it sprays and hits a person's body,

The heat of the yang energy
is not merely the ferocity of melting iron;
the yin energy striking it

the striking energy hitting people

Now, thunder
is fire,

If the marks from the burn look like writing,

If all people have transgressions,

clearly writing out the reason for the punishment,

The "Chart" emerged from the Yellow River,

Lightning writing is not evident,

If that is the case,
the traces of fire burning

Vain and deceitful customs
love to create strange and bizarre things.
How to verify that lightning is fire?
If a person is struck by lightning and dies,

If the head is struck, then the beard and hair will be burnt.
If the body is struck, then the skin will be scorched.

Practitioners of Daoist arts believe that lightning

When a person is harmed by the cold,

the abdomen, being originally warm,

this is the third proof.
During a thunderstorm,
flashes of lightning are frequently seen,
and a large fire, like a person shining,

When lightning strikes,
at that time,
it sometimes burns down people's houses and even the grass and trees on the ground –
this is the fifth proof.
Thus, the argument that thunder is fire has five proofs;
the claim that thunder is the anger of Heaven has no evidence whatsoever.
Therefore, the idea that thunder is the anger of Heaven
is empty and false.
Someone might object, saying:

What the *Lunyu* (Analects) refers to,

Why is this?
Because it is not for oneself.
If indeed one fears thunder,

Why is this?
What the thunder strikes
is mostly people without fault.
The gentleman fears encountering it by chance,

Now, if this is the case,
the gentleman's movements

To punish all those who are not good.

The *Rú Shū* (Book of the Confucians) says:

One like Lú Áo.

How much more likely then, that Lú Áo 盧敖, all alone,

This is no different from the words of Xiàng Màndū 項曼都 of Púbǎn 蒲坂 in Hédōng 河東.

Suddenly, I seemed to be lying down,
The people of Hédōng called him a dismissed immortal.

what reason would he have to return?

Fù Yù (復育) transformed into a cicada;

it could not transform back into Fù Yù (復育).
Things that can ascend
all possess wings;
if they ascend and then descend again,

Have you seen wings on Màn Dū's (曼都) body?

Perhaps Màn Dū (曼都) admired the Dao,

Ashamed and without words,

His meaning was to say that the Dao could be learned,
